title: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept
body:
Read the chapter → [Isaiah 28](/bible/isaiah/28)

**[Isaiah 28:1-4](/bible/isaiah/28#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/isaiah/28#v1)</sup> Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine!
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/isaiah/28#v2)</sup> Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one, which as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm, as a flood of mighty waters overflowing, shall cast down to the earth with the hand.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/isaiah/28#v3)</sup> The crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, shall be trodden under feet:
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/isaiah/28#v4)</sup> And the glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley, shall be a fading flower, and as the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up.

- Woe to the crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower; pride sits on them like a crown.
- The Most High has a mighty and strong one, like a tempest and a flood of mighty waters, that shall cast down to the earth with the hand; this is the northern kingdom being brought down in its rulership because of pride, refusing the things of the Bible. The crown of pride is trodden under feet.

**[Isaiah 28:5-8](/bible/isaiah/28#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/isaiah/28#v5)</sup> In that day shall the Lord of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people,
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/isaiah/28#v6)</sup> And for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/isaiah/28#v7)</sup> But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/isaiah/28#v8)</sup> For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.

- In that day the Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the residue of His people, the remnant that escapes the judgment, and a spirit of judgment to those who sit in judgment.
- The priests and prophets err through wine and strong drink and are out of the way; they are not drunk on the law of God but on the philosophies of men, and today this is the pastors and the politicians who err with lies and philosophy and love it. Their tables are full of vomit, so all the religions today are full of vomit and there is no place clean.
  - **[Micah 2:11](/bible/micah/2#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/micah/2#v11)</sup> If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.

    A man walking in falsehood who prophesies of wine and strong drink is the prophet this people want; the people err in lies and philosophies like Christianity and politricks.

**[Isaiah 28:9-13](/bible/isaiah/28#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/isaiah/28#v9)</sup> Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/isaiah/28#v10)</sup> For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little:
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/isaiah/28#v11)</sup> For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/isaiah/28#v12)</sup> To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/isaiah/28#v13)</sup> But the word of the Lord was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little; that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.

- Whom shall He teach knowledge and make to understand doctrine? Them that are weaned from the milk, for doctrine is the law of God. The method is precept upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little; a scripture must be laid upon another scripture, for the Bible is a puzzle in the Old and New Testaments that must be unfolded and put together along with keeping God's laws.
- With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people; off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law the oppressor's culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. This Bible is the rest and the refreshing, yet they would not hear, so the word came precept upon precept that they might fall backward and be broken and snared.
  - **[Proverbs 4:2](/bible/proverbs/4#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/proverbs/4#v2)</sup> For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.

    The Most High gives good doctrine; the doctrine to be understood is the law.
  - **[Isaiah 33:19](/bible/isaiah/33#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/isaiah/33#v19)</sup> Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand.

    When Israel keeps the law they shall not see a fierce people of a deeper, stammering speech they cannot understand.
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:49](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v49)**
    > <sup>[49](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v49)</sup> The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand;

    The curse: a nation swift as the eagle whose tongue thou shalt not understand, which is America and the white man, whose culture was repeated and beaten in.
  - **[Matthew 15:24](/bible/matthew/15#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/matthew/15#v24)</sup> But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

    Christ says He was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, yet Christianity answers with John 3:16.
  - **[Matthew 5:17](/bible/matthew/5#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/matthew/5#v17)</sup> Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.

    Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it, yet they twist "fulfil" to mean He abolished it.

**[Isaiah 28:14-18](/bible/isaiah/28#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/isaiah/28#v14)</sup> Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/isaiah/28#v15)</sup> Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/isaiah/28#v16)</sup> Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/isaiah/28#v17)</sup> Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding place.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/isaiah/28#v18)</sup> And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it.

- Woe to the scornful men that rule this people in Jerusalem, who say they have made a covenant with death and with hell; today's leaders have made a covenant with captivity and killing, and the mega churches financed by the government are nowhere to be found when the people get killed on the front lines. They say they have made lies their refuge and hidden under falsehood, for they love lies.
- Therefore the Most High lays in Zion a tried stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation, which is Christ and this Bible; He lays judgment to the line and righteousness to the plummet, and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies so their covenant with death is disannulled.

**[Isaiah 28:19-22](/bible/isaiah/28#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/isaiah/28#v19)</sup> From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you: for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/isaiah/28#v20)</sup> For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/isaiah/28#v21)</sup> For the Lord shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/isaiah/28#v22)</sup> Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong: for I have heard from the Lord God of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth.

- When the overflowing scourge passes through, the leaders shall be trodden down by it; their bed is too short to stretch on and their covering too narrow to wrap in, so their lies will not be their refuge when judgment comes.
- The Most High shall rise up as in mount Perazim and be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon to do His strange work; therefore be not mockers, for a consumption is determined upon the whole earth.
  - **[2 Samuel 5:20](/bible/2-samuel/5#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/5#v20)</sup> And David came to Baal–perazim, and David smote them there, and said, The Lord hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal–perazim.

    As the Most High broke forth upon the Philistines at Baal-perazim, so shall He do this strange act.

**[Isaiah 28:23-29](/bible/isaiah/28#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/isaiah/28#v23)</sup> Give ye ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/isaiah/28#v24)</sup> Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/isaiah/28#v25)</sup> When he hath made plain the face thereof, doth he not cast abroad the fitches, and scatter the cummin, and cast in the principal wheat and the appointed barley and the rie in their place?
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/isaiah/28#v26)</sup> For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/isaiah/28#v27)</sup> For the fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/isaiah/28#v28)</sup> Bread corn is bruised; because he will not ever be threshing it, nor break it with the wheel of his cart, nor bruise it with his horsemen.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/isaiah/28#v29)</sup> This also cometh forth from the Lord of hosts, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working.

- Give ear and hear: the plowman does not plow all day but breaks the clods, casts abroad the fitches and cummin, and sets the wheat, barley, and rye each in its place, for his God instructs him to discretion and teaches him.
- The fitches and cummin are beaten out with a staff and a rod, not threshed with a heavy instrument or a cart wheel, and bread corn is bruised only so far; this also comes forth from the Lord of hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in working, showing the measured instruction God gives.
